model: Regulated-utility dividend discount at cost of equity with exit multiple (engine route; rate-base compounding, net debt zero)

inputs.base_revenue_note: ENGINE MAPPING: the 'revenue' slot carries ADJUSTED (non-GAAP) OPERATING EARNINGS TO COMMON for FY2026E = guidance midpoint $2.88 x 1,037M fully diluted shares = $2,987M. Guidance $2.85-$2.91 narrowed 2026-10-30 from $2.81-$2.91 (EXC_Analysis.json guidance block). FY2025 adjusted operating EPS $2.77; GAAP diluted $2.73 (net income $2,768M, 10-K). 9M-2026 GAAP diluted EPS $1.98 vs $2.15 (Q3-2026 10-Q :14077-14078) -- GAAP is running ~$0.15-0.20 below adjusted in 2026 because of the Pepco Maryland rate-case write-offs and BGE project impairments; the bear path treats such 'non-recurring' disallowances as a recurring drag.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at the current price: 1,035M shares outstanding at 2026-09-30 (Q3-2026 10-Q balance sheet :14205; Q3 basic weighted average 1,035M) + 2M treasury-stock-method shares on stock-based awards (:14073-14074, diluted 1,037M). The $1.0B 3.25% Convertible Senior Notes due 2029 convert at $57.11 with principal settled in cash (:17542-17548), so they add nothing at the current price; the ~16.5M shares under outstanding ATM forward sale agreements (forward prices $43.17-$48.68, maturities Nov-2026 to Sep-2027, :18180-18199) were antidilutive at Q3 and add <0.5M under the treasury-stock method today. Held FLAT in the engine because growth_rates are PER-SHARE adjusted EPS growth: management's 5-7% algorithm is per share and already nets the ATM/forward equity programme (~$1.0B remaining on the ATM, :18200-18202). Per-share values do not depend on this count; only the headline equity total does.
inputs.net_debt_note: Held at ZERO by construction: the discounted stream (dividends) is post-interest, so the $53.2B of debt is already serviced inside earnings; deducting it again would double-count (dcf-methods SKILL.md: never FCF / WACC on a post-interest flow). Debt and cash below are recorded for audit only.
inputs.total_debt_note: 2026-09-30 Exelon consolidated (Q3-2026 10-Q :14178-14191): short-term borrowings $934M + long-term debt due within one year $1,078M + long-term debt $50,791M + long-term debt to financing trusts $390M = $53,193M. Year-end 2025 was $50,080M on the same definition (Metrics CSV FY2025 TotalDebt 51,093 includes other items).
inputs.cash_note: Cash and cash equivalents $1,469M at 2026-09-30 (:14142); restricted cash $602M excluded.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026E dividends declared to common = $0.42 x 4 = $1.68/share (all four 2026 quarterly dividends declared at $0.42, Q3-2026 10-Q :19719-19722; up from $0.40 in 2025 and $0.38 in 2024) x 1,037M = $1,742M. This is the FY0 flow the engine compounds. Reported owner FCF is NOT the stream (see reported_fcf).
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2025 reported FCF = OCF $6,254M - capex $8,529M = -$2,275M (Metrics CSV). 9M-2026: OCF $5,404M - capex $6,799M = -$1,395M (Q3-2026 10-Q :14109-14111). Structurally negative through the ~$41B 2026-2029 capital plan ($9,950M in 2026, $31,300M 2027-2029; 10-K :22498-22506), which is projected to add ~$23B to rate base by end-2029 and earns allowed ROEs of 10.35-11.50% (10-K :21331-21338). An unlevered owner-FCF DCF would value the equity at ~nothing -- a method artefact (AIA.NZ, ES, EVRG, AEP, ETR precedents), not a finding.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K Note 18, total stock-based compensation expense included in O&M $41M (2024 $34M, 2023 $21M; :28520). SBC is 0.17% of revenue and is EXPENSED inside both GAAP and adjusted operating earnings (Exelon's adjusted EPS does not add it back), so sbc_pct_path is 0 and house = street. Equity-award taxes are not separately disclosed and are immaterial at this scale.
inputs.interest_income_note: Interest income from affiliates is $11M (10-K :29076) and the company is a large net borrower; nothing to strip, and the stream is post-interest anyway.
inputs.buyback_note: No repurchases since FY2008 (kpis.buybacks). Exelon is a net ISSUER: ~16M shares via the ATM in 2025 at ~$43.24 average, ~2.3M in Q3-2026 at ~$43.29, forwards outstanding for ~16.5M more, and ~37% of 2026-2029 equity needs pre-priced (EXC_Analysis.json). The dilution is netted inside the per-share growth path.
inputs.wacc_rationale: The 'wacc' field is the COST OF EQUITY (7.75%), because the stream is dividends out of post-interest earnings. USD build: 10-year UST 4.86% (Yahoo ^TNX close 2026-11-06, as used for the ES/EVRG/AEP builds the same weekend) + regulated-utility equity beta ~0.55 x ERP 5.0-5.5% = 7.6-7.9%; 7.75% taken. Below AEP/Eversource (8.0%) because Exelon is a T&D-only, largely revenue-decoupled utility with no generation or fuel exposure; not lower than 7.75% because of BBB+/Baa2 holdco leverage ($53B debt on $30B book equity), the six-regulator political mosaic and the 2026 wave of state legislative intervention. Identical across the three scenarios: risk is charged once, through the paths and weights, not through per-scenario discount rates. Cross-check: allowed ROEs are 10.35% (PECO) to 11.50% (ComEd formula, 10-K :21331-21338); the market pays ~1.57x book ($45.62 / $29.05 BVPS at 2026-09-30) and ~15.8x FY2026E adjusted EPS at a 3.7% dividend yield, consistent with a market cost of equity near 7.3-7.8%.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable: operating leases are immaterial (lease interest $6M/yr at the parent, 10-K :26088) and inside O&M, hence inside earnings.
inputs.nci_treatment: None: Exelon has no material non-controlling interests after the 2022 Constellation separation; earnings used are attributable to common shareholders.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE. Exelon is a pure-play rate-regulated electric and gas T&D holding company (ComEd, PECO, BGE, Pepco, DPL, ACE; no generation since the Feb-2022 Constellation spin): earnings = allowed ROE x the equity layer of rate base, and growth comes from capex that regulators admit to rate base (~$41B 2026-2029, ~7.9% rate base CAGR, +$23B by 2029). dcf-methods/SKILL.md has no utility row; the operating-company row (owner-FCF DCF) is wrong here because reported FCF is structurally negative by design (FY2022-FY2025: -2,277 / -2,705 / -1,528 / -2,275; 9M-2026 -1,395) while the capex that drives it earns a regulated return above the cost of capital -- the firm-level DCF would be >100% terminal value against $53B of debt and return negative equity for a company earning ~9.5% on book. Per the skill's principle ('discount the flow the business actually produces, at the rate appropriate to whom it accrues') and the folder precedent for regulated utilities built this week (ES, EVRG, AEP; ETR on FCFE; GPT.AX/GMG.AX for the engine pattern), the model is a DIVIDEND DISCOUNT at cost of equity run through the engine: revenue slot = adjusted operating earnings to common; growth_rates = per-share adjusted EPS growth (nets the ATM/forward equity issuance); ebitda_margin_path = dividend payout ratio, so engine FCF = dividends to common; sbc/D&A/capex/tax paths = 0 (all inside earnings); wc_capture 0; net_debt 0; terminal = min(Gordon on year-10 dividends at CoE, 25x year-10 dividends). Dividends, not earnings, are the stream because the ~40% retained is what funds the growth already in the EPS path; capitalising earnings would count it twice. Exelon's stated policy is a ~60% payout of adjusted operating earnings, so the payout path converges on 60%. CROSS-CHECK: the base-case terminal Gordon multiple (1.03/0.0475 = 21.7x dividends at a 60% payout) implies a ~13x exit P/E on year-10 EPS, below today's 15.8x forward; the valuation is deliberately not assuming today's multiple persists. Terminal growth is 3.0% in the base (vs 3.5% at EVRG/AEP) because Exelon has the lowest rate-base growth of the batch and the most acute affordability backdrop (Maryland rate-case moratorium, Delaware capex cap, PECO's withdrawn rate case, NJ/MD transmission-adder complaints). FY0 is FY2026E (guidance midpoint), so Y1 = FY2027. SEC XBRL has not indexed the Q2/Q3-2026 10-Qs (Metrics CSV stops at Q1-2026); the Q3-2026 10-Q TEXT is extracted and was used for every anchor above.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Management's long-term adjusted operating EPS target of 5-7% through 2029 (midpoint taken; Q3-2026 call said tracking near the top end), corroborated by the 3-year GAAP diluted EPS CAGR of 7.8% (FY2022 $2.18 -> FY2025 $2.73), the 3-year adjusted operating EPS CAGR of 6.9% ($2.27 -> $2.77) and the 3-year DPS CAGR of 5.8% ($1.35 -> $1.60).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity (book) CAGR of 5.2% diverges >30% from the EPS CAGR of 7.8% over FY2022-FY2025. Expected for a regulated utility: per-share earnings compound on RATE BASE growth and allowed ROE while book equity grows at retention plus ATM issuance; the per-share EPS path, not book-value growth, is the right driver here. Equity CAGR is not used.
historical_growth.notes: All 3-year CAGRs run FY2022-FY2025, the first three full years after the Feb-2022 Constellation separation. 5-year revenue uses the restated continuing-operations FY2020 base ($16,663M -> $24,258M); 5-year EPS and equity CAGRs are null because FY2020 figures include the generation business (equity fell from $34.9B to $24.7B at the spin). 5-year DPS CAGR is 0.9% only because the dividend was reset from $1.53 to $1.35 at separation; it has grown 5-6%/yr since. FCF CAGRs are null: reported FCF is negative in every year FY2022-FY2025 (capex 1.3-1.6x OCF by design), so a CAGR is undefined and SBC-adjusting it ($21-41M/yr) changes nothing material. Revenue growth overstates the economics because purchased power and gas are pass-throughs.

base.narrative: Adjusted EPS grows 6.5%/yr FY2027-FY2029 off the $2.88 FY2026E midpoint, landing FY2029 at ~$3.48 -- a 5.9% CAGR off FY2025's $2.77, i.e. the middle of management's 5-7% range rather than the 'top end' they are tracking toward, haircut for the ComEd Grid Plan decision (the 2024 plan was cut ~25%), the Maryland moratorium and the GAAP-vs-adjusted gap. Growth then fades 5.5% -> 3.0% by year 10 as the 2026-2029 plan rolls off. Payout drifts from 58.3% (FY2026) to the 60% policy level, so dividends grow ~6.5-7%/yr near-term then with EPS.

bull.narrative: The top of the range is delivered: the ICC approves the 2028-2031 ComEd Grid Plan near the ~$15.3B ask in Dec-2026, the ~11 GW 'high probability' data-centre load in northern Illinois converts to transmission and substation rate base, the $350M 2027 O&M programme lands, and BGE's Jan-2027 Maryland order is constructive. EPS compounds 8%/yr FY2027-FY2029 (FY2029 ~$3.63, the 7% top-end CAGR off 2025), then fades to 3.5%. Payout holds at the 60% policy.

bear.narrative: The affordability backlash compounds: the ICC cuts the Grid Plan by a quarter again, Maryland extends the moratorium and strips the transmission adders, Delaware's capex cap and PECO's deferred rate case leave ~$5-8B of the plan unrecovered on time, the data-centre pipeline keeps shrinking (43 -> 36 -> ~23 GW) and the Pepco/BGE-style write-offs recur, so adjusted EPS grows only 2% in FY2027 and 4%/yr to FY2029 (FY2029 ~$3.18, a 3.5% CAGR off 2025, below the 5% floor). The board keeps raising the dividend ~5%/yr for two years, pushing payout to 62% before it is held there; terminal growth 2.5%. Still a solvent, investment-grade, dividend-paying utility -- the downside is a lower growth rate and a lower multiple, not impairment.

scenario_narratives.base: Exelon compounds rate base at ~7-8%/yr through 2029 but converts it to ~6% per-share EPS growth after ATM dilution, interest headwinds and partial regulatory disallowance; the dividend follows the 60% payout policy. Discounted at a 7.75% cost of equity with 3.0% terminal growth, the base case prices the stock at roughly 13x year-10 earnings -- below today's ~16x forward multiple, so the model is not paying for multiple expansion.
scenario_narratives.bull: The grid-investment and data-centre thesis is delivered in full: a near-ask ComEd Grid Plan, constructive Maryland and FERC outcomes, large-load rate base beyond the plan, and the O&M programme push EPS to the 7% top of the range through 2029 with a durable 3.5% tail.
scenario_narratives.bear: Six jurisdictions' affordability politics bite at once -- a second Grid Plan cut, an extended Maryland moratorium, lost transmission adders, a shrinking data-centre pipeline and recurring write-offs -- leaving EPS growth at 3-4% while the capital plan is funded anyway. The dividend is safe; the growth premium is not.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 25/50/25 rather than the house 15/50/35. Bear is lifted to 25% because the thesis sits on a binary regulatory outcome (ICC decision on the ~$15.3B ComEd Grid Plan, mid-December 2026, after the prior plan was cut ~25%), three state legislatures intervened against Exelon utilities in 2026 alone, the data-centre pipeline has been revised down three times, and 2026 GAAP earnings are tracking ~$0.15-0.20 below adjusted on 'non-recurring' write-offs. Bull is cut to 25% because it requires several independent things to go right at once (near-ask Grid Plan, constructive Maryland/FERC rulings, large-load conversion, cost programme delivery). No going-concern or covenant risk, so bear is not pushed higher.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A regulated T&D utility is a compounder of rate base at an allowed ROE funded by retained earnings, debt and new equity; the only cash an outside shareholder receives is the dividend, so the model discounts dividends per share at the cost of equity with net debt at zero, and lets the terminal value be the lower of Gordon growth and a 25x dividend (~15x earnings) cap. Reported FCF is ignored as a valuation input because it is negative by design during a capital supercycle. The main judgement is the per-share EPS path -- whether the 5-7% algorithm survives the ComEd Grid Plan decision and the 2026 affordability legislation -- and the result should be read as the price at which a 7.75% equity return is earned, with the 15% hurdle entry price far below it as it is for every low-growth bond-proxy.
key_risks_to_valuation: ComEd Grid Plan (2028-2031, ~$15.3B) decision at the ICC, expected mid-December 2026: the 2024-2027 plan was cut ~25%; ComEd is ~29% of revenue and the fastest-growing utility in the group.

State legislative intervention: Maryland Utility Relief Act (forecast-test-year moratorium to April 2027, RTO mandate triggering transmission-adder complaints), Delaware SB 326 capex cap on DPL, New Jersey RTO mandate for ACE.
Data-centre load conversion: pipeline trimmed 43 GW -> 36 GW -> ~23 GW; only ~11 GW 'high probability' and ~4 GW collateralised.
Dilution and leverage: ~$1.0B ATM capacity, ~16.5M shares under forwards, ~63% of 2026-2029 equity needs still to price; $53B debt at BBB+/Baa2 with collateral triggers below investment grade.
Interest rates: a 100bp move in the cost of equity moves the base value by roughly 20-25% (see sensitivity grid); the 10-year UST at 4.86% is the anchor.
GAAP-vs-adjusted gap: Pepco Maryland write-offs, BGE impairments and the ComEd FERC audit show disallowances recur; the model anchors on adjusted EPS and carries that risk in the bear weight.
FERC PJM cost-allocation re-calculation back to 2015 with interest (Oct-2026 order): impact not yet estimable, could be material.
ComEd's City of Chicago franchise is terminable on one year's notice with a municipalisation option -- a structural tail risk not in any scenario.
